course_name_original: INSTALACIONES INDUSTRIALES Y EN EDIFICIOS I
prerequisites: Proficiency in computer packages, word processors, excel spreadsheets

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve practical application cases in different types of buildings; single-family homes, multi-family homes, offices, hotels and sports centers.
Ability to synthesize and concretize the operation, design and calculation of water and solar thermal installations.
Awareness of the impacts of building installations on the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
Mastery of standards, elements, equipment and systems for water and solar thermal installations for domestic hot water (DHW).
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of Industrial and Building Installations.
Project-based learning with an approximation to professional reality.
Commitment to environmental preservation and sustainability.

syllabus_topics: Fundamental concepts: flow, pressure and pressure drop
Pressure losses in pipes and fittings
Installation elements: pipes, valves, taps and others
Water lifting installations and pressure booster sets
Selection of pumps and auxiliary equipment
Pressure booster sets for water lifting, variable speed and constant speed
Example of design and calculation of water installation in a single-family home
Example of design and calculation of water installation in a multi-family residential building
Example of design and calculation of water installation in hotels and office buildings
Domestic Hot Water Installations in Buildings: DHW
Purpose, Description and Regulations. Thermal Installations in Buildings Regulation (RITE), components and installation diagrams
Production and distribution of domestic hot water
Heat generation equipment for domestic hot water installations: instantaneous heaters, combi boilers, floor-standing boilers, heat pumps
Minimum Contribution of Renewable Energy for DHW: HE4
Introduction, energy situation and energy sources
Solar thermal energy: collection using collectors
Example of design and calculation of DHW installation with solar support in a residential building
Example of design and calculation of DHW installation with solar support in a hotel
Example and calculation of swimming pool heating with solar support
Regulations: CTE Health Document HS 5 Water Evacuation
Example of design and calculation in residential buildings, hotels and office buildings

assessment_methods.method: Written exam Block 1 (Plumbing, DHW, and HE4)

assessment_rules: To pass the course, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required for all assessed activities and blocks in both ordinary and extraordinary calls. In progressive evaluation, all thematic blocks and associated practices must be approved. Practices not passed during progressive evaluation must be resubmitted for the global exam. Blocks and practices passed in the ordinary call remain valid for the extraordinary evaluation. The overall grade will be the higher of the one obtained through progressive evaluation during the semester and the one corresponding solely to the final global exam. For the global exam, Block 1 and Block 2 each account for 50% of the grade. The extraordinary evaluation also consists of Block 1 (50%) and Block 2 (50%).
